title: Into the Fire
subtitle: But I don't have a choice.

items.text: After breakfast, several Yao gather around Mayfly's bed.

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: Mayfly, you were out for the whole day!

items.speaker: Hedgehog
items.text: Brother Yam told me you were unwell, so I brought some sweet cakes. I thought you might like something to eat after your fall.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Hmm. Thank you.
Still half-asleep, Mayfly responds in a weak voice.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Mayfly, it's me again.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I've brought herbs to replenish your Qi. Don't worry. I checked. All cut from plants. No Yao were harmed.

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: Greetings, Grandmaster!
The Yao greet her enthusiastically. She nods to each of them in turn, then sets a bundle of herbs on the table.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Ah, no need for those formalities, please. Would you give Mayfly and me a moment in private?

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: Of course. We'll leave you two alone.

items.speaker: Yam
items.text: Don't you hear the grandmaster? Come on, let's go.
The Yao nudge each other out of the room. Before long, only Paper Heron and Mayfly remain.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Paper Heron?
She senses something unusual about the moment and turns her head to find Paper Heron wearing a dour expression.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Mayfly, you must stop practicing Rén's method.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Why?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Your Qi is too unstable. At times, it surges like a boar, and at others, it falters. Haven't you noticed?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You know I'm right, don't you? Your fall before was a warning. Your Qi is in decline.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: But I've felt so much more energetic lately. Even my mind feels clearer than before.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Yes. You have learned a great deal about how to control your Qi. You'd be in great shape, if that were all you were practicing.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: For you to advance further, your Qi must align with the Way, and your body must be strong enough to carry it.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: But if you're too weak, your Qi can become too great a burden. It could consume you.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: In the White Horse School, we always ensured our physique was strong enough to handle each step along the path.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: But Rén is moving too fast, pushing you forward with the power of the Longevity Sword. It's possible you may still succeed in the end, but ...

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You're risking both body and spirit for a tiny possibility.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You could end up with nothing. Your body destroyed, your spirit extinguished. You need to stop and allow your body to recover.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: For how long? Days? Weeks? Months?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Given your condition, I'd say two months before you resume any training.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Two months?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Do you realize how little time I have? Winter's coming. I can't wait that long.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I know.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: But if you continue in this fashion, I fear you may not live to see the winter.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I can't stand by and watch you destroy yourself. Not just you. All the Yao. This isn't the right path for any of you.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Heron ...

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I know, to you, two months may seem like nothing. I suppose it may seem like years pass you by in the blink of an eye, don't they?
Paper Heron gazes at the girl propped halfway up in bed. Her lips tremble faintly before she finally speaks.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: It's not quite as fleeting as a blink of an eye.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: What would you do over the course of a year?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I—

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Wander the roads on your mule, through cloud-covered mountains, across gentle streams, beneath fragrant blooming peach trees.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: And when the year ends, you'd go to Huanzhou for the temple fair, feeling the warmth of the flames dancing against your face, savoring the floral sweetness of sticky rice cakes.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Next year you'll travel further still, to see snow-covered plains, brush the fur of a moose, taste wine so strong that it burns your throat.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: You never worry about the days you spend on the road or whether you have enough time to experience all the world has to offer.
The words hang bitterly on her lips, soon accompanied by wet tears flowing down her face.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: But I won't live a full cycle of seasons.
One drop, two drops, three drops. The bedding covering her grows damp with a steady flow of tears.
Paper Heron can do nothing to stem their flow. So, she simply waits, watching her friend in tender silence.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: To you, a day, a month, a year, it means nothing.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: But for Yao like me, a year is a lifetime—our only lifetime.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I want to live, even just a little longer, to see more, feel more. I can't allow myself to waste even a moment.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: In a thousand years, my name could still be carved on that stone. But I won't live to know if it's there next spring. So, why must you stop me?
There are barbs on the question, too sharp to swallow, too true to ignore. She chews on it a long while, hoping to reach an answer.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I didn't intend to hurt your feelings when I carved that stone.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Is it your wish then? To live as long as the stones?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: What? What do you mean?
Paper Heron smiles, but a trace of sorrow lingers at the corners of her mouth.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Besides Inner Alchemy and Rén's method, there is a third way to escape the flow of time, one that has been kept a secret.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: It doesn't take hundreds of years of training, nor does it endanger your Qi. All it costs is your school, a sword, and a hundred years sealed in a tree.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: When the seal breaks, all you once knew will be gone—friends and enemies alike. You will no longer laugh nor hate, and your senses will dull.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Sweet or sour, salt or spice, it will all taste the same.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: People will cheer at the blazing fire flowers, yet to you, the flames will be as mild as a passing breeze, their excitement like a language you no longer understand.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Your memories will stay. You'll always recall how the morning mist felt on your face, the crispness of spring water as it flowed through your fingers, but you will never feel them again.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You will become like a stone. Is that what you want?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Is that how the world feels to you?
She doesn't reply.
Mayfly lowers her head, her fingers twisting together as if trying to hold the weight of her tangled thoughts.
After a moment's consideration, she takes something from her pocket.
It's the amulet that was trampled by her and repaired by Paper Heron.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: But Heron, you've already shown me a way.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: This amulet—I spent every coin I had on it, just for a chance to get through the city gate.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: It didn't work like I'd hoped, and I felt so foolish for believing in it. But you repaired it, even improved it, so that I could make it through.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I may be just a wind-tossed reed, but that doesn't mean I'm unworthy of the wonders of this world. Isn't that what you wanted to tell me?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I'm willing to take the chance to lose everything or gain the world.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: You once said that fate presents an opportunity to every one of us.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: You've had yours, and I need to take mine.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You mean that you want to follow Rén's method no matter the danger?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Yes.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: *cough* She-She has shown us a way to live beyond our years.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Even if it's dangerous, I want to take the chance to truly live.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I understand.
She knows it won't be useful to argue her point any longer. She rises to her feet and taps the herbs on the table.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Just remember to drink my herbal brew, eh?
The door stands ajar. Other Yao peer inside with curiosity. Paper Heron walks past them without a word.
In the dazzling morning light, she walks straight toward the courtyard.
